examples.name: Default
examples.summary: One frame at the default `video` ratio. The source is the reserved `example.com` page standing in for a real demo. Only an `http` or `https` URL is framed: a `javascript:`, `data:` or relative `src` renders the title as plain text instead, and the frame is always sandboxed (scripts, forms, popups and presentation only, no top-level navigation). Change `ratio` and the frame changes shape without the page shifting, because the ratio is reserved before the document loads. `title` has no default on purpose — an `iframe` without one is announced as an unnamed frame, and a screen-reader user meets that name before any content.

examples.name: Ratios
examples.summary: Every `ratio` value, one frame under the other, around the same placeholder document. Each frame keeps its shape at any width — only the height follows. Pick the ratio the source already has: a `video` frame around a square form leaves bands of empty surface above and below it, and no ratio will crop a document that disagrees, it will just scroll inside the frame. Each frame states its own `title`, because every embedded document needs its own name.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same content written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<Embed>` tag into a real `Embed`. Braced attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry and never imports the component.

examples.name: Page JSON
examples.summary: The same content in the marketing site's page JSON: `Embed` is a scene, so a band places it by name in its `scene` slot (here `console-showcase-section` with `variant: "diagram"` and `texture: "none"`, so nothing is painted behind it) and `SitePage` renders the entry with no code.
